title: Harpoon Logistics onramp scratchbook
body:
Quick capture from 2025-02-12 kickoff with Harpoon Logistics (raw–notes to tidy later)

Attendees: Priya K (Redwood), Dana C (Redwood, solution lead), Ethan W (Harpoon ML), Marta R (Harpoon CTO), Lucas G (Harpoon infra)
Recording: asked to avoid recording (sensitive PII in example payloads) — we have written consent for redacted snippets only.

1) High-level ask
- Harpoon wants an LLM-powered routing assistant for freight exceptions + customer messaging.
- Primary constraints: private data governance, sub-200ms p95 generation for 256-token responses, predictable cost for Q3 scale (est. 150–300 req/s peak).
- Preference for Redwood Dedicated behind VPC peering; evaluate Private (VPC) for later on-prem spinoff.

2) Requirements (as described by Harpoon) — raw
- Network: VPC peering to their AWS account; no open internet egress from inference tier.
- Auth: SSO (SAML) for console access + KMS integration (customer-managed CMK) for keys.
- Data residency: EU (for EU customers) + US for operations; need region routing policy.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for critical route with canary fallback to hosted models if Dedicated capacity exhausted.
- Throughput/latency: aim p95 <200ms for 256 tokens, average token length ~180 chars per reply, typical prompt size 120–400 tokens.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, traceable per-request metadata (shipment_id, tenant), alerting for model-quality regressions (drift on top-1 intent).
- Security: audit logs to their SIEM, optional private audit endpoint, no logs retained by Redwood beyond 30 days for pilot.

3) Demo payloads / data quirks they showed
- Mixed language (EN/ES) in same prompt — important for tokenizer mismatch experiments.
- Lots of short structured fields (addresses, shipment ids) + long freeform descriptions — impacts KV cache benefits and batching shape.
- Example payloads had newline-delimited JSON wrapped in text blobs; they sometimes include escaped control chars.

4) Gotchas / risks flagged in call
- NAT + egress flow: Lucas warned their security team will block unknown egress IP ranges; need precise outbound IP list for peering and testing windows.
- Token accounting: They do intent-scoring + reranks (3 variants) which multiplies token-per-action; cost estimates from commercial quoting may undershoot real usage by ~2.5x.
- Cold KV cache on canary fallback will spike latency — need a warmup strategy or progressive rollout.
- Model hallucination risk on customer-sensitive statements (pricing penalties) — they want guardrails and rollout with human review on high-risk classes.
- On-prem interest: they want to pilot Dedicated first, but there's an active RFP for air-gapped eventuality — catalog requirements for that path differ (no outbound telemetry).

5) Engineering notes (things to validate)
- Sizing: estimate GPU pool for 200 req/s at p95<200ms for 256 tokens. Run back-of-envelope with our continuous-batching profile + their token distribution (Ethan to share sample distribution).
- Model choices: start with an MPT-family quantitative baseline + Redwood-verified curated candidate (we should propose 2 model flavors: high-throughput quantized & higher-accuracy fp16).
- Batching: configure max_batch_ms low to preserve latency; but allow burst buffer for cost. Need guidance from runtime SRE on safe defaults.
- KV/prefix caching: experiment with per-tenant prefix cache (customer uses tenant-per-request). Evaluate memory impact on Dedicated nodes.
- KMS flow: confirm CMK cross-account grant pattern. Ops to write step-by-step for Lucas.

6) Action items / owners (first pass)
- Priya: assemble pilot SOW draft + proposed milestones (due 2025-02-19).
- Dana: lab-run sizing matrix + two model candidates (due 2025-02-23).
- Ethan (Harpoon): share anonymized token distribution + 10 redacted sample payloads (by 2025-02-17).
- Lucas (Harpoon): confirm VPC peering window and egress firewall rules (by 2025-02-20).
- Infra (Dana + SRE): produce outbound IPs list and peering checklist doc (link to be added).

7) Pilot plan (sketch)
- Week 0 (prep): network + KMS handshake, SSO config, Confluence SOW sign-off.
- Week 1–2 (bench): deploy Dedicated test pool in us-west-2 + eu-west-1 (mirror), run synthetic traffic with token dist, measure p50/p95.
- Week 3 (canary): roll out to 5% production traffic for non-critical routes; human review on flagged responses.
- Week 4–6 (run): iterate on model config, quantization, batching; on-call support for hotfix.
- Goal: go/no-go decision for larger reserved capacity by end of week 6.

8) Open questions to answer in follow-up
- How much of their event stream must be logged to their SIEM vs retained by Redwood? (privacy/legal)
- Do they require in-line de-identification? If so, where in the stack (client side vs proxy)?
- Acceptable cost per 1k tokens for pilot vs committed contract — need concrete number to model economics.
- Will they allow a small telemetry channel for quality monitoring if on-prem air-gapped becomes mandatory later?

9) Misc notes / idiosyncratic points
- Marta is explicitly worried about misattributing penalties in customer messages — suggested a "human in the loop" confidence threshold for charge-related messages.
- Ethan: wants ability to pin model weights per-tenant for A/B tests (we should note versioning ergonomics).
- They use a home-grown retriever that returns structured fields; integration point could be a pre-processor hook instead of embedding store migration.

10) Next meeting: schedule follow-up technical deep-dive w/ SRE + security (30–45m). Proposed attendees: Lucas (Harpoon infra), Dana (Redwood SRE), Miguel (Redwood security). Tentative window: week of 2025-02-24.

Notes-to-self: keep this as scratchbook — will produce cleaned SOW + concise risk table for Marta. Try to surface quantitative cost scenarios rather than percent multipliers. Include sample cURL snippets for peering test and minimal demo payload sanitized for PII.

End of scratch capture.
